fields.title: 1. Event — Starship Flight 15 (Starlink Group 31-2)
fields.md:
### 1-1. Primary record (④ launch record)

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Launch | **2026-11-13 22:47:36 UTC** · Orbital Launch Pad 2 | ④ [LL2 launch record](https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0/launches/0f867f0c-5422-4d44-93b8-d7faaae7019b/), retrieved 2026-11-14 |
| Status | **'Payload Deployed'** (outcome not finalized) · last updated 2026-11-14 02:11:54 UTC | Same as above |
| Booster landing record | **Failure** — no return to the launch site was attempted; stopped before the landing burn and splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico | Same as above |
| Ship landing record | Attempt planned · result null · Ship status 'Active' | Same as above |
| Mission description (pre-launch plan wording) | 15th test flight · fourth V3 · second Starlink deployment · first Ship return-to-launch-site attempt · about 275 km · 14 orbits · over 22 hours | Same as above |
| Previous flight | Flight 14 — 2026-09-28 · 'Launch Successful' | ④ [LL2](https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.4.0/launches/7d1afb26-6f9c-429b-9ccf-29012fd1e519/) |

### 1-2. Flight progress (⑤·⑥ press reports — to be verified)

| Stage | Details | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Booster B22 | A catch at Pad 2 was planned about 6.5 minutes after launch. The catch was canceled for 'undisclosed reasons' and the booster was diverted to the sea, where it exploded and disappeared from view | ⑥ [Spaceflight Now 11/13](https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/11/13/live-coverage-starship-flight-15-attempts-to-recover-full-vehicle-in-double-launch-pad-catch/) |
| Booster (AP) | It fell into the Gulf of Mexico after an automatic abort. A photo caption said it exploded after being diverted to the water | ⑤ [AP·PBS 11/13](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/science/spacexs-starship-soars-into-orbit-after-booster-malfunction-thwarts-double-catch-attempt) |
| Ship 42 | Reached orbit · deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites · up to 14 orbits | ⑥ Spaceflight Now |
| Ship return plan | 22.5 hours after launch, about **21:20 UTC (11/14)** = 11/15 06:20 KST. If anomalies occur, alternative splashdown off Hawaii or Chile | ⑥ Spaceflight Now |

### 1-3. 'West Coast flight halt' reports — cross-check against sources

| Time (HST, 11/13) | Details | Source |
|---|---|---|
| About 10:50 | FAA nationwide ground stop (domestic flights to and from the US mainland) — cause was a **air traffic control communications problem** (reported) | ⑥ [Hawaii News Now](https://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/2026/11/14/faa-lifts-nationwide-ground-stop-what-hawaii-travelers-should-know/) |
| 13:55 | Hawaii Department of Transportation (HDOT) post: 'All west coast flights have been halted due to debris from SpaceX launch' | Same as above · ⑥ [KHON2](https://www.khon2.com/local-news/faa-grounds-u-s-travel-hdot-director-says-hawaii-trips-continue/) |
| About 15:20 | Nationwide ground stop lifted. HDOT said the temporary halt due to debris was also lifted | Same as above |

- **Not used in the verdict**: The explanation of the debris cause rests on a single state transportation department post. This round's search did not find an FAA Debris Response Area (DRA) issuance or a mishap designation. The booster fell in the Gulf of Mexico off Texas and the Ship was in orbit. So the path of any West Coast impact is not explained by the original sources → logged under T3 check ③ (source: table above · `state.triggers_next_12m[T3]`).

### 1-4. Filings and company materials

- **No SpaceX 8-K or IR** — the latest EDGAR filing is the **11/13 SC 13G/A**. Founders Fund, Peter Thiel and 32 others in total reported 3.8% of Class A (314,357,058 shares, event date 9/30, denominator 8.24 billion Class A shares), falling below 5%. The filing before that is the 11/06 8-K (5.02) (source: ① [EDGAR filing list](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json) · ① [13G/A original](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000142601226000007/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml), retrieved 2026-11-14).
- The 13G/A is a simple investment report and not a milestone input. It also does not touch the volume in the lock-up table (T2) (source: `state.triggers_next_12m[T2]`).

**Verdict**:

1. **R2 (Ship recovery success by 2027-06)**: **Not triggered** — the recovery attempt has not yet happened. The verdict is made only from the finalized LL2 result and the company's official summary. Whether 'recovery success' counts only a tower catch, or also an undamaged splashdown and reusable condition, will be fixed as the first task of the next run, **before the result is out** (source: `state.probability_adjustment_rules` R2 · `state.open_questions_for_next_run`).
2. **B-2027-1 (orbital insertion + at least 1 Ship recovery, 2027)**: Remains in progress. Orbital insertions go **from 1 to 2** (Flight 14·15), and Ship recoveries stay at **0**. Loss of a booster is not counted by this milestone (source: `state.milestones` B-2027-1 · table 1-1).
3. **B-2027-2 (12 Starship flights per year, 2027)**: Remains in progress. The 2026 reference value goes **from 3 to 4** (5/22·7/24·9/28·11/13) (source: `state.milestones` B-2027-2 · LL2).
4. **The booster explosion** is not a milestone input. It is recorded only as background to the reuse-economics argument. The cause and whether the FAA investigates await official records (source: table 1-2).
